_readme: The Free SWFT Growth Guide (Customer Journey Check). One source for the web check (guide-worksheet.html via js/journey-check.js) and the PDF (npm run build:guide-pdf). Question text may use {action}, {actionNoun}, {proof}, {relationship} from the chosen industry. No research figures here on purpose: only add a statistic after checking the original source, date, population and scope.
title: The SWFT Growth Guide
promise: Find where customers get stuck. Know what to fix next.
disclaimer: Based on your answers; not an independent audit.

industries.label: Professional services
industries.action: send a qualified inquiry or book a consultation
industries.proof: relevant work, fit, process and expectations
industries.outcomeHint: Long sales cycle? Track qualified conversations now and review revenue later.

industries.label: E-commerce
industries.proof: product detail, authentic imagery, and delivery and returns clarity
industries.outcomeHint: Count completed orders, not just sessions or add-to-carts.

industries.label: Restaurants
industries.action: reserve, order or plan a visit
industries.proof: a current menu, atmosphere, location and hours
industries.relationship: return visits and the right occasions to reconnect
industries.outcomeHint: Compare the same days of the week; seasons and events move covers.

industries.label: Community & events
industries.proof: the purpose, the hosts, practical details and what to expect
industries.outcomeHint: A registration is not attendance: track who actually shows up.

outcomes.label: Less time on a manual task

stages.title: Found
stages.question: Can I find you when I need what you offer?
stages.intro: Choose one audience, one offer and the places people use to discover it. Start with the paths your customers actually use.
questions: Do you know where recent customers first discovered your business?
Do your main discovery profiles clearly explain who you help, what you offer and where you serve?
Are the important details and links on those profiles accurate?
Are you publishing or maintaining useful material that answers your audience's real questions?
Can someone move from discovering you to the relevant offer in one clear step?
stages.firstAction: Follow your most important discovery path on a phone. Correct one missing detail, unclear description or broken next step.
stages.evidence: Relevant visits or inquiries by source. Where tracking is limited, start asking new customers how they found you.
stages.obstacle: people who need what you offer may not be finding you, or may not reach the right offer
stages.help: Discovery strategy, local visibility, photography, video and content connected to the offer.

stages.title: Trust
stages.question: Is this right for me, and why should I choose you?
stages.intro: Explain the outcome, show credible proof and help the right person understand the fit. Your difference should be specific enough to demonstrate.
questions: Can a new visitor quickly explain what you offer, who it is for and why it matters?
Do you explain a meaningful reason to choose you and show evidence for it?
Can people see authentic work, experiences, reviews or other relevant proof, such as {proof}?
Can they understand the buying process, key expectations, and the price or how to get a quote?
Does the experience on a phone make that information easy to read and use?
stages.firstAction: Rewrite the main offer statement and place a relevant piece of proof beside it. Ask someone unfamiliar with the business to explain the offer back to you.
stages.evidence: What test visitors understand, recurring pre-sale questions, and movement from the offer page to the intended next step.
stages.obstacle: visitors may not understand the offer quickly or see enough proof to choose you
stages.help: Positioning, offer messaging, visual storytelling, case studies and website experience.

stages.title: Take action
stages.question: Can I take the next step easily, and do I know what happens afterward?
stages.intro: Make one main action clear. Check the entire path, including the confirmation, response and handoff.
questions: Is there one clear way to {action} on the page or profile for this offer?
Can a customer complete it on a phone without a broken link, unnecessary field or confusing instruction?
Do they receive confirmation and know what happens next?
Is someone responsible for each {actionNoun}, with a response expectation the business can meet?
Do you record completed actions and follow through to the next business outcome, such as a qualified conversation or fulfilled order?
stages.firstAction: Run a clearly marked test {actionNoun}. Check receipt, confirmation, routing and follow-through. Use a test mode for paid transactions where available.
stages.evidence: Completed actions divided by relevant visits or starts, response time where relevant, and qualified inquiries or fulfilled orders. Show counts alongside rates.
stages.obstacle: interested people may not be able to {action} easily, or the handoff after it may break
stages.help: Booking and checkout journeys, forms, integrations, routing and useful automation.

stages.title: Come back
stages.question: Was it worth it, and why would I return or recommend you?
stages.intro: Retention starts with delivering what was promised. Follow-up should support that experience and offer a useful reason to reconnect.
questions: Do customers receive the delivery, onboarding or experience you promised?
Is there a consistent way to check satisfaction and resolve problems?
Do you ask for a review or referral at an appropriate moment?
Is there a relevant next offer, reminder or invitation for people who want it?
Can you identify {relationship} over a period that fits your business?
stages.firstAction: Map the first follow-up after the customer receives value. Give it an owner, a trigger and a useful purpose.
stages.evidence: Rebookings, repeat purchases, referrals or repeat participation over an appropriate period; unresolved issues; owner time spent on the workflow.
stages.obstacle: customers may not get a reason, or a reliable experience, to come back or recommend you
stages.help: Onboarding, customer communications, review workflows, reactivation and reporting.

plan.title: Understand
plan.text: Walk the journey as a customer. Confirm the obstacle, record the baseline and choose one priority. If there is too little activity to judge, start collecting evidence and extend the review period.

plan.title: Improve
plan.text: Make the smallest useful change. Assign a person responsible for it and test the complete path.

plan.title: Connect
plan.text: Make the handoff dependable: define the trigger, the next action, the owner, and what happens if something fails. Automate stable, repetitive steps where useful.

plan.title: Review
plan.text: Compare the same measures across comparable periods. Note changes in traffic, seasonality, promotions or capacity that may also explain the result. Keep, revise or stop the change, then select the next priority.

card: The customer I want to help
The outcome I want to improve
How I will test that it works
What happened and what I learned
example: Illustrative only: a service business receives inquiries, but some never reach the person responsible for booking. First verify receipt and response history. Then connect the inquiry to a named owner, send a confirmation and set an overdue reminder. Check that every test inquiry reaches the right place. Review qualified bookings, missed inquiries, response times and administrative time. The workflow is complete when the handoff works; evidence of transformation comes from the customer and business experience over time.

progress.label: Built
progress.text: The page, content or automation exists.

progress.label: Working
progress.text: Customers can use it and the workflow completes reliably.

progress.label: Improving the business
progress.text: The customer or operating outcome changes in a useful way.
